A few more questions.

Read the guide
Do both machines need to be on the same network?

No. iroh tries a direct connection across networks and uses the built-in Tokyo relay when needed. Reachability depends on network conditions. Direct-only mode is available; custom relays are not currently supported.

Can I keep using my existing serial tools?

Yes, through a local mapping. macOS and Linux use a PTY; Windows needs a compatible com0com driver and port pair. PTYs do not forward DTR/RTS. Hardware flow control and continuous BREAK are not currently supported. Test your specific tools and hardware.

Can the relay read my serial data?

The relay forwards end-to-end encrypted data and cannot decrypt serial content. It can observe metadata such as IP addresses, connection times and traffic volume. Device private keys are stored in restricted local files, not the system keychain.

Do serial sessions reconnect automatically?

A disconnected serial session currently needs to be reconnected manually. Network path selection does not provide automatic serial-session reconnection.

Are logs uploaded or kept indefinitely?

Logs stay on your machine. Each session retains up to 500 entries or 128 KiB; you can export records still in the buffer. Pausing freezes the display, not collection.

Does resetting identity revoke access on every machine?

No. Resetting clears local pairings. You must remove the old device manually on other machines. There is no central account recovery, so keep your device keys safe.
